# Settings API

The app's settings, as the dashboard's **Settings** shows them. All endpoints are for **superusers**.

## Read the settings

`GET /api/settings`

```json
{
  "meta": { "appName": "Acme", "appURL": "https://acme.example.com", "senderName": "Support", "senderAddress": "support@acme.example.com", "hideControls": false, "accentColor": "#1055c9" },
  "smtp": { "enabled": true, "host": "smtp.example.com", "port": 587, "username": "acme", "authMethod": "", "tls": false, "localName": "" },
  "s3": { "enabled": false, "bucket": "", "region": "", "endpoint": "", "accessKey": "", "forcePathStyle": false },
  "backups": { "cron": "", "cronMaxKeep": 3, "s3": { "enabled": false, "bucket": "", "region": "", "endpoint": "", "accessKey": "", "forcePathStyle": false } },
  "batch": { "enabled": false, "maxRequests": 50, "timeout": 3, "maxBodySize": 0 },
  "rateLimits": { "enabled": false, "rules": [] },
  "trustedProxy": { "headers": [], "useLeftmostIP": false },
  "logs": { "maxDays": 5, "minLevel": 0, "logIP": true, "logAuthId": false, "maxDataSize": 0 },
  "superuserIPs": []
}
```

Secrets (`smtp.password`, the `s3` secrets) are never sent back; send them only to change them.

## Change the settings

`PATCH /api/settings`

Send only the sections and keys you change; the answer is the full settings:

```bash
curl -X PATCH http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/settings -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"meta": {"appName": "Acme"}, "batch": {"enabled": true}}'
```

## Send a test email

`POST /api/settings/test/email`

| Body | |
|---|---|
| `email` | where to send it |
| `template` | `verification`, `password-reset`, `email-change`, `otp` or `login-alert` |
| `collection` | optional: the auth collection whose template to use (default `_superusers`) |

Answers `204` once the mail server took it.

## Check S3

`POST /api/settings/test/s3` with `{"filesystem": "storage"}` (or `"backups"`) tries the saved S3 settings for files
or backups; `204` if they work, `400` with the reason if not.

## Apple sign-in secret

`POST /api/settings/apple/generate-client-secret` makes the client secret Sign in with Apple needs, from `clientId`,
`teamId`, `keyId`, `privateKey` and `duration` (seconds), and answers `{"secret": "..."}`.
